title: Dev server started with debug=True and bound to 0.0.0.0
evidence: app.py:159 `app.run(debug=True, host='0.0.0.0', port=5000)`; README.md documents `python app.py` as the run command
suggestion: Default to debug=False (or read from an env var) and bind to 127.0.0.1 — the Werkzeug debugger exposes an interactive console to anyone who can reach the port

title: Tests share the service's on-disk books.db and never reset it
evidence: app.py:8 `DB_FILE = 'books.db'` is a fixed relative path; test_app.py:11 the `client` fixture only calls `init_db()` — no tmp_path, no DELETE/teardown, so rows accumulate across runs
suggestion: Parameterize DB_FILE (env var or app config) and point the fixture at a tmp_path/in-memory database so tests are isolated and repeatable

title: requirements.txt omits pytest although the tests import it
evidence: requirements.txt contains only `flask`; test_app.py:1 `import pytest`, and README.md:Testing says `python -m pytest test_app.py -v`
suggestion: Add pytest to requirements.txt (or a separate requirements-dev.txt) so the documented test command works from a clean environment

title: The ?author= filter has no test
evidence: app.py:74-78 implements the filter, but no test in test_app.py issues a request with an `author` query parameter (only bare `client.get('/books')` at test_app.py:58)
suggestion: Add a test that creates books by two authors and asserts GET /books?author=... returns only the matching subset

title: init_db() runs only under __main__, so a WSGI import leaves the table uncreated
evidence: app.py:157-158 calls `init_db()` inside `if __name__ == '__main__':`; no module-level or before-request initialization — importing `app` (as any WSGI server does) skips schema creation
suggestion: Call init_db() at import time, or on first request, so the schema exists however the app is started

title: Validation checks key presence only — empty or non-string title/author are accepted
evidence: app.py:43 `if not data or 'title' not in data or 'author' not in data` (same check at app.py:106); POST {"title": "", "author": ""} is stored as a valid book, and `year` is never type-checked
suggestion: Reject blank/whitespace-only title and author, and validate that year is an integer, before inserting

title: ?author= is a substring LIKE match, not an exact match
evidence: app.py:78 `SELECT * FROM books WHERE author LIKE ?` with `f'%{author_filter}%'`
suggestion: None required — TASK.md does not specify the semantics; noting it because runs differ here and it affects cross-run comparability
